question: Does the native DLR 140 m cube, reduced by pixel-area mean to the prepared 4096 x 2048 map, change what the Monochrome lens shows compared with the pinned WMS render of the same product?

current.origin: USGS WMS layer Ceres_FC_global, 4096 x 2048, 0-360 E

values.note: No ISIS Null (0) pixels. Under the WMS render's south-polar gap the native mean is 1.0, so the cube stores that gap as 1, the same value as clipped shadow elsewhere (11.1% of all pixels).

method: Tile rows streamed from the cube (2.7 MB each). Native pixel-area mean onto the WMS frame (0-360 E, 90 N-90 S); 0 excluded. Pixelmatch threshold 0.1, includeAA. The same WebP q80 lane applied to both for the delivered comparison.

pixelScaleEnergy.note: The WMS render has 14% more pixel-scale energy than the area mean and less than native nearest sampling.

image: wms-vs-native.webp: rows 71.7 S 131.8 E and 14.4 N 240.8 E (Occator); columns current WMS map, native area mean, pixelmatch difference; 200 x 200 map pixels at 3x.
conclusion: Same product, same prepared size, same tone and registration. Between 34 N and 11 S, 0.1-0.4% of pixels change; outside it 1.3-19% change, most toward the poles (16-19% between 45 S and 79 S), where the WMS render shows resampling jaggies that the area mean does not. No resolution is gained.
